feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is claimed for it. Evidence: iteration 9 (five 12 mm sensors at x -0.02 to +0.02 m, y 0.06 m, mass 0.8, wheel_radius 0.03, wheel_track 0.12, controller kp 3.0, kd 0.2) scored 52.985, the best so far. Oval progress rose to 0.151 and s-bend progress fell to 0.140 compared with iteration 0 at y 0.05 m (0.138 and 0.148). Line loss stayed at 1.0 per run on oval and s-bend and at 2.0 on slalom. Steering oscillation stayed between 0.10 and 0.14, so the robot is not jittering. Iterations 1 to 3 showed that 16 mm sensors and y 0.03 m lowered progress without removing the loss, and iteration 8 showed that an 8 mm footprint lowers progress on all tracks, so 12 mm is the footprint to keep. Iterations 5 and 6 showed that the wheel change does not help. What I had to compensate for: the forward row sees the tape earlier, so the controller had to keep kp 3.0 and kd 0.2 to hold the line; the controller was not changed to suit the offset. Decision rules for the next race: (1) If the s-bend loss stays at the same point as iterations 0 and 7 (late sensing on the tightest bend) and steering_oscillation stays below about 0.2, the forward offset is useful, and the next geometry test is y 0.055 m. (2) If the s-bend loss moves earlier, or the s-bend progress drops below 0.140, return to y 0.05 m, which gave the best s-bend progress. (3) If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2, the forward lead is causing lag-driven overshoot. Stop moving y forward and treat the geometry as at its limit; the remaining lever is the controller.
requested_changes: Keep five 12 mm sensors at x -0.02 to +0.02 m, with sensor y at 0.06 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, wheel_track 0.12 m and mass 0.8 kg. Basis: iteration 9 gave the best score (52.985), with oval progress 0.151 against 0.138 at y 0.05 m, and the loss stayed at a single event per run.

If the next race shows the s-bend loss at the same progress point and steering_oscillation below about 0.2, try sensor y 0.055 m with everything else unchanged. Basis: iteration 0 (y 0.05 m) gave s-bend progress 0.148 and iteration 9 (y 0.06 m) gave 0.140, so an intermediate offset may keep most of the oval gain while recovering s-bend progress.

If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2 at y 0.06 m, return sensor y to 0.05 m and do not move the offset further. Basis: oscillation was 0.07 to 0.14 across iterations 0 to 9, so a jump above 0.2 would show that the forward lead is causing lag-driven overshoot.
